Class Game

java.lang.Object
chess.service.Game
public class Game extends Object
Coordinates a two-player game: owns the board, the players, and the turn, and decides whether a requested move is allowed.

This class contains no console input or output, so the Phase 2 GUI can call exactly the same methods from its event handlers.

Simplified rules in this prototype

  • Check, checkmate, stalemate, castling, and en passant are not implemented.
  • Because check is not enforced, a king can be captured; capturing the opposing king ends the game and that player wins.
  • Pawn promotion: see handlePromotion(Position).

  • Method Details

    • start

      public final void start()
      Starts (or restarts) the game: sets up the board, clears history, and gives White the first move. Declared final because the constructor calls it; an overridable method called from a constructor could run in a subclass before that subclass is initialized.

    • end

      public void end()
      Ends the game without declaring a winner (for example, when a player quits).

    • tryMove

      public MoveResult tryMove(Position from, Position to)
      Attempts to move the current player's piece from one square to another.

      Checks are applied in this order, and the first failure is reported: game over, same square, empty source, wrong owner, friendly destination, movement pattern, blocked path. If any check fails, the board and the turn are left exactly as they were.

      Parameters:
      from - source square; must not be null
      to - destination square; must not be null
      Returns:
      a MoveResult describing success or the reason for failure

    • handlePromotion

      private String handlePromotion(Position square)
      Applies this prototype's last-rank rule for a pawn that just moved to square.

      Simplified rule: the pawn is always promoted to a queen of the same color; the player cannot choose another piece. This limitation is documented in the README.

      Parameters:
      square - the destination square of the move just made
      Returns:
      a note to append to the move description, or null if nothing happened
